cues.en: Good afternoon, everyone. And what can I say after that? I'm going to try to be a little hasty here because times are passing and we have, as I say, some sound production coming after us here. Art and opinions are shown here in multiple colors and shades because that's really what they are. It's whatever you want it to be. Art is whatever you want it to be.
cues.zh: 大家下午好。刚才那些之后，我还能说什么呢？我得讲得快一点，因为时间在流逝，而且就像我说的，后面还有声音制作环节。艺术和观点在这里以多种色彩和深浅呈现，因为它们本来就是这样。它取决于你想让它成为什么。艺术就是你想让它成为的样子。

cues.en: opinions are, whatever they happen to be. But I come from the science side of things. It's black and white. It's reality. It's there or it's not there. If it's good, if it's accurate, it's repeatable. You can do it today, tomorrow, here, or in Timbuktu and get the same answers. Science is different from art. Science is different from opinions. And yet, they go together. They must go together, in fact. If they don't, we will fail at our...
cues.zh: 观点呢，就是它们碰巧成为的样子。但我来自科学这一边。科学是黑白分明的。它是现实。要么存在，要么不存在。如果它是好的、准确的，它就可重复。你今天做、明天做、在这里做，还是在廷巴克图做，都会得到同样的答案。科学不同于艺术。科学不同于观点。然而，它们相辅相成。事实上，它们必须相辅相成。否则，我们就会在……

cues.en: our enterprise of entertaining the world with wonderful art. Sound production, the real thing happening on stage like this, it is art in real time, and two performances may never be exactly the same. That's just what, that's what it is. Sound reproduction, you put two letters in front of it, R-E, and the world changes because you're going to try to capture a performance, artistically craft it and save it.
cues.zh: 用精彩艺术娱乐世界这项事业上失败。声音制作，像这样在舞台上真实发生的东西，是实时的艺术，两场演出可能永远不会完全一样。就是这样，这就是它的本质。声音重放，你在前面加两个字母 R-E，世界就变了，因为你要捕捉一场演出，从艺术上精心处理并保存下来。

cues.en: so that somebody somewhere, sometime, can press a play button. And if everything works right, they will hear what you've created. Sadly, that is rarely the case. Most of the time, what people hear in their homes, in their cars, through their earbuds or whatever, is not what the artists hear or anywhere else created. I think it's a shame.
cues.zh: 这样，某个人在某个地方、某个时候就能按下播放键。如果一切正常，他们就会听到你创造的声音。遗憾的是，这种情况很少见。大多数时候，人们在家里、车里、耳机里或别处听到的，并不是艺术家听到的声音，也不是他们在任何地方创作出来的声音。我觉得这很可惜。

cues.en: I think it's nice when you go to an art gallery, they make sure that the lighting is correct so that the colors on the paintings will be as close as possible. At least put the artists created. They don't put amber lights on or blue lights on. They put neutral north light on. What's wrong with this picture? Well, it just simply says that a lot of research has been done on concert halls, some on workspaces because human health is involved.
cues.zh: 我觉得这很好：你去美术馆时，他们会确保灯光正确，让画作上的颜色尽可能接近艺术家创作时的样子。他们不会用琥珀色灯或蓝色灯，而是用中性的北向光。这张图有什么问题？它只是说明，人们对音乐厅做了大量研究，对工作场所也做了一些研究，因为这涉及人类健康。

cues.en: homes and cars and headphones, not so much. But where do we listen? It's the other way around. That's where we are entertained. We go to concerts, but not that often. We listen at home, we listen in our cars, we listen through headphones. I don't know how much, but certainly the trend is right. And in fact, if you think about marketing of products and sound, I mean, if you think of, would you look at that? I love that because...
cues.zh: 家里、车里和耳机里，就没那么多研究了。但我们到底在哪里听？情况正好相反。那才是我们娱乐的地方。我们会去听音乐会，但没那么频繁。我们在家里听，在车里听，用耳机听。我不知道比例有多大，但趋势肯定是对的。事实上，如果你想想产品和声音的营销，我是说，如果你想到——你看那个？我很喜欢那个，因为……

cues.en: Here is 1918, is Thomas Edison claiming that he has created a reproduction device that will imitate a human being or a violin. And this is a blind test that you'll notice that some of the blindfolds cover the ears. So it's a blind and partially deaf test, and maybe that's how he got away with it.
cues.zh: 这是 1918 年，托马斯·爱迪生声称他发明了一种重放设备，可以模仿人声或小提琴。这是一次盲测，你会注意到有些蒙眼布还遮住了耳朵。所以这是一次又盲又部分失聪的测试，也许他就是这样蒙混过关的。

cues.en: But no, back then and between then and now there have been several demonstrations of live performers beside loudspeakers reproducing live performers. And the audiences would be amazed that they couldn't tell the difference. Well, you wonder, you know, have we made no progress in the hundred years since Thomas Edison? Of course we have. It's just that.
cues.zh: 但不是这样。在那之后直到现在，已经有过好几次演示：现场表演者站在重现现场表演者的扬声器旁边，而观众惊讶地发现，他们根本分辨不出两者的区别。你可能会想，一百年过去了，从 Thomas Edison 以来，我们难道一点进步都没有吗？当然不是。只是……

cues.en: It's slick marketing, it's a good party trick, let's just say that. In the case of the concert hall demonstrations, I might just add, I suspect there's good, strong evidence to indicate that it's the hall that makes the difference. If they were to do that test in anything other than a really good hall, it wouldn't perform, it wouldn't resolve, it wouldn't work as well. Okay, if you get science involved, and we have to pay serious attention, we're gonna do listening tests, they're not just sitting around with your
cues.zh: 这就是高明的营销，说到底，也算是个不错的派对技巧。在音乐厅的演示中，我还想补充一点：我怀疑有充分而有力的证据表明，真正产生差异的是音乐厅本身。如果把这个测试放在一个真正优秀的音乐厅以外的任何地方进行，效果都会打折扣，解析力也不够，表现不会那么好。好，如果把科学引入其中，我们就必须认真对待它。我们要进行听音测试，而不是随便坐在那里，端着你喜欢的

cues.en: drink of choice with listening to your music of choice, it's actually hard work. That requires preparation and concentration. If you do it right, under the right circumstances, you get something that I call subjective measurements because the results from the listeners are highly repeatable, very consistent with standard deviations of the same kind as you get out of technical measurements.
cues.zh: 饮料，听着你喜欢的音乐。这其实是件很辛苦的工作，需要准备和专注。如果做得正确，并且条件合适，你就能得到一种我称为“主观测量”的结果，因为听众给出的结果高度可重复，标准差也与技术测量所得的标准差属于同一水平。

cues.en: If you're going to do technical measurements, they have to be accurate, otherwise they lie to you, and they have to be comprehensive, otherwise they're not telling you all of the truth. And so that is a requirement that eliminates an awful lot of people in our business from the game, because they don't have the facilities to do these highly precise technical measurements. I have been fortunate, both at the National Research Council and at Harman, to have access to wonderful
cues.zh: 如果要进行技术测量，测量结果必须准确，否则它们会误导你；还必须全面，否则它们无法告诉你全部真相。因此，这个要求会把我们行业里的很多人挡在门外，因为他们没有条件进行这种高度精确的技术测量。我很幸运，无论是在 National Research Council 还是在 Harman，都能使用出色的

cues.en: to make measurements, and dedicated listening rooms to do subjective evaluations. And if you do both of those things and start comparing the results, you very, very quickly see patterns. They're not difficult. They're obvious. They just stand up and shout at you. But there are certain things you do in a loudspeaker, and if you do those, people give it the thumbs up right away. They love it. If you don't do those things, then you're just taking the big gamble you don't want to take.
cues.zh: 测量设备，以及专门用于主观评估的听音室。如果同时做好这两件事，再开始比较结果，你会非常非常快地发现其中的规律。这些规律并不难发现，它们显而易见，简直会直接站起来对你大喊。但在扬声器上，有些事情你必须做到；做到这些，人们马上就会竖起大拇指。他们会非常喜欢。如果做不到，那你就是在冒一个根本不该冒的大风险。

cues.en: So let's talk about listening to us first. It's the single most important and really the most difficult factor in achieving this understanding of the relationship between what we measure and what we hear. There are lots of opinions around, my goodness, just pick up any audio magazine, onto any audio website, enter any forum on the topic. You will find opinions of all colors and flavors.
cues.zh: 所以，我们先谈谈听音。这是理解测量结果与听感之间关系时，最重要、也最难处理的单一因素。关于这件事，观点多得很。天哪，随便拿起一本音频杂志，打开任何一个音频网站，进入任何一个相关论坛，你都会看到各种各样、五花八门的观点。

cues.en: They really just are noise in the background. Some of them may be right, but you don't know which ones. So we need methods that turn opinions into facts. First thing we do is we make it blind. It's obvious. You just disguise what the person is listening to. So they can't see the brand, the price, the size, and remember what their favorite reviewer said about it, what have you, that kind of thing. We make the test double blind.
cues.zh: 它们其实只是背景杂音。有些观点可能是对的，但你不知道是哪些。所以我们需要把主观看法转化为事实的方法。我们做的第一件事就是做盲测。这很显而易见。只要把受试者在听什么掩盖起来就行。这样他们就看不到品牌、价格、尺寸，也想不起自己喜欢的评测人说过什么等等这类东西。我们把测试做成双盲的。

cues.en: If you're a scientist, so then you know that you, the experimenter, me, the experimenter, I am not influencing the result by the sequence in which I'm presenting these sounds or anything as obvious as that. It has to be randomized and in fact the tests that we've done for years are randomized by a computer. We just press go and go have a cup of coffee. Test is done by the computer. So it is truly double blind.
cues.zh: 如果你是科学家，你就会知道，你作为实验人员，我作为实验人员，并没有通过呈现声音的顺序或任何类似显而易见的方式来影响结果。它必须是随机的，事实上我们多年来的测试都是由计算机随机控制的。我们只需按下开始，然后去喝杯咖啡。测试完全由计算机完成。所以这才是真正的双盲。

cues.en: You have to make sure the test, sorry, the sounds you're comparing are equally loud. We do a multiple comparison test, so you're not just comparing one with another. It's certainly not the take home and listen to it kind of test that reviewers do, because that teaches nothing. You learn really nothing from that, except that you might be able to adapt to its problems or not adapt to its problems. Only when you compare one thing with another.
cues.zh: 你必须确保测试——抱歉，是确保对比的声音响度完全一致。我们做的是多重对比测试，所以不是简单的一对一对比。这绝对不是评测人那种“拿回家听听”的测试，因为那样根本得不出任何结论。你从中真的什么都学不到，除了你可能会慢慢适应它的毛病，或者适应不了。只有通过相互对比，

cues.en: to start to realize what differences there may be. And if you do a simple A versus B comparison, and both A and B share the same problem, you won't hear that problem. So it's nice to have C and maybe D to mix things up a little bit. It seems obvious, looking back on it, all I can say is that I'm very fortunate that the first listening test I ever did
cues.zh: 才能开始发现可能存在的差异。如果你只做简单的 A 和 B 对比，而 A 和 B 有同样的毛病，你是听不出这个毛病的。所以最好有 C，甚至 D，来把变量搞丰富一点。现在回想起来这似乎显而易见，我只能说我非常幸运，我平生做的第一次盲听测试，

cues.en: of 1966 or 1967 was a three or four-way test, and I've just been doing it ever since. But now we know that it's probably the preferred way of doing things. So the listener controls which one of these speakers is active, and when you're doing these comparisons, you do them one at a time, in monophonic, one speaker, not stereo, not multi-channel. Why? Well, because it just turns out that
cues.zh: 也就是在 1966 或 1967 年那次，就是一个三路或四路对比测试，从那以后我就一直这么做。而现在我们知道，这大概是最好的测试方式。受试者可以控制哪只音箱发声，在做这些对比时，每次只听一只，采用单声道、单只音箱，不是立体声，也不是多声道。为什么？因为事实证明，

cues.en: The more people are listening to stereo, the less critical the listener is of the loudspeaker itself.
cues.zh: 听众在听立体声时，对音箱本身的挑剔程度反而会降低。

cues.en: But we have to pay attention to mono because it's a reality in television and movies. Most of the sound comes monophonically from the center front loudspeaker. It is the most important loudspeaker in the whole room because all the dialogue comes from it. Most of the on-screen sounds come from it only in high-budget blockbuster movies do they bother to pan anything. So we do the test in mono and
cues.zh: 但我们必须重视单声道，因为电视和电影里处处都是单声道。大部分声音都是以单声道形式从中置音箱发出来的。它是整个房间里最重要的音箱，因为所有对白都来自它。画面上的大多数声音也都来自它，只有在高成本大片里，他们才会费心思去做声像平移。所以我们用单声道进行测试，而且

cues.en: We occasionally have done comparisons in stereo as well, just to prove the point to questioning persons. And every time, the ones that win the mono tests win the stereo tests. There has been no exception to that rule. There is nothing special about stereophony or multichannel, as far as sound quality is concerned. So here's a person, one person at a time. They just sit there and listen to music and...
cues.zh: 我们偶尔也会做立体声对比，只是为了向心存疑问的人证明这一点。每一次，在单声道测试中胜出的音箱，在立体声测试中也一样胜出。这个规律从未有过例外。就音质本身而言，立体声或多声道并没有任何特殊之处。所以这里坐着一个人，一次只测试一个人。他们就坐在那里听音乐，然后……

cues.en: press which of A, B, C, or D they want to listen to. They make notes. The notes are compiled in the computers. The music is in loops, so it's easy to make these comparisons over a period of time. Every time the music changes, the speakers associated with each of the A, B, C, D codes also changes. So each time the music changes, it's a whole new experiment. A person at no time knows what's behind the screen.
cues.zh: 按下 A、B、C 或 D，选择想听哪个。他们做记录。记录由电脑汇总。音乐是循环播放的，所以在一段时间内做这些比较很容易。每次音乐变化，与 A、B、C、D 各代码对应的扬声器也会变化。所以每次音乐一变，就是一个全新的实验。测试者始终不知道屏幕后面是什么。

cues.en: Here I've removed the screen and the bottom picture. And you can see that there are three loudspeakers in that test. Only one of them is in the forward active position. It takes about three seconds to exchange. It's all hydraulically driven and computer controlled, cost of fortune, and paid willingly. Why bother? Why do we bother spending that money?
cues.zh: 这里我移除了屏幕和下方图片。可以看到那个测试里有三个扬声器。只有一个处于前方工作位置。切换大约需要三秒。整套系统是液压驱动、电脑控制，造价不菲，而且是我们心甘情愿花的钱。何必费这个劲？我们为什么非要花这笔钱？

cues.en: going through all this rigmarole of blind and double-blind and all that sort of thing. Well, because it matters. People are fickle. Humans are desperately fickle. We offer up opinions of what we're listening to, which are different if we see what we're listening to. To prove that point, when I joined Herman, nobody there could ever remember having done a blind test. Not a single blind test, even.
cues.zh: 要经历盲测、双盲测试这一整套繁琐流程。嗯，因为它很重要。人是善变的。人类极其善变。我们会对自己听到的东西发表意见，但如果能看到听的是什么，意见就会不同。为了证明这一点，我加入 Herman 时，那里没人记得做过盲测。甚至连一次盲测都没有。

cues.en: They were all professionals, I was told. And as a professional, they're not biased by what they see. They really know what good sound is. And so because they know what good sound is, they can do these tests without any complications of blind screening and so on. So Sean had just joined the company at the time, Sean Olos, my colleague from NRC and McGill. Now Dr. Sean Olos.
cues.zh: 我被告知，他们都是专业人士。作为专业人士，他们不会因为看到的东西而产生偏见。他们真正懂得什么是好声音。所以，正因为他们懂得什么是好声音，他们做这些测试时不需要盲测筛选之类的复杂流程。当时 Sean 刚加入公司，Sean Olos，我在 NRC 和 McGill 的同事。现在是 Dr. Sean Olos。

cues.en: Anyway, what we did was just to bring in some of these professional listeners and some others and put them through a battery of tests. Not everybody wanted to do it.
cues.zh: 总之，我们做的就是请来一些这样的专业听音员和其他一些人，让他们接受一系列测试。不是每个人都愿意做。

cues.en: There were a couple of holdouts. They felt that they had nothing to lose if their reputations as golden years were so high that they didn't want to threaten that reputation. Anyway, in these blind tests, we had four loudspeakers. Two were rated very highly. These were visually identical speakers. They differed only in their crossover designs.
cues.zh: 有几个坚持不参加的人。他们觉得，如果自己作为“金耳朵”的名声已经那么高，就没什么可失去的——可他们不想拿这名声冒险。总之，在这些盲测中，我们有四个扬声器。其中两个评分很高。这两个扬声器外观完全相同。它们只在分频器设计上不同。

cues.en: There it is. This test, the speaker down here, is a little $700 subset system. Disgustingly good for $700. Just disgustingly good. It wouldn't play as loud as the other ones, but if you kept the sound levels at good foreground, listening level and not pushing it too hard, it just...
cues.zh: 就是这个。这个测试里，下面这个扬声器是一套 700 美元的小型系统。对于 700 美元来说，好得离谱。就是好得离谱。它不会像其他几个那么响，但如果你把音量保持在合适的前景聆听水平，不要推得太狠，它就……

cues.en: It cooked. It was a good system for $700. These others were $5,000. So here's the US competitor. Beautiful wooden cabinet, sculptured looking, wonderful, $4,000. And in the blind tests, we had two winners and two not so good ones. We let them see what they're listening to, and the loyal Harmon employees gave these ones even higher scores, of course, because they were beautiful, and they were big, and they were Harmon products.
cues.zh: 它很给力。对 700 美元来说，这是一套好系统。其他这些是 5000 美元。所以这里是美国竞争对手。漂亮的木制箱体，雕塑感外观，很棒，4000 美元。而在盲测中，我们有两个赢家和两个不太好的。我们让他们看到自己在听什么，忠诚的 Harmon 员工当然给这些扬声器打了更高的分，因为它们漂亮、个头大，而且是 Harmon 的产品。

cues.en: This little one was a Harman product too, but they could never overcome the bias that it was so small and plastic, that something small and plastic could not sound good. And so they reduced its score. The competitor did a little better because they could see it now and it had this beautiful cabinet. And so they gave it a little more, but even then they felt that it wasn't quite up to the Harman product.
cues.zh: 这个小家伙也是 Harman 的产品，但他们始终克服不了一个偏见：它太小、太塑料，这么小又这么塑料的东西不可能好听。于是他们给它打了低分。竞争对手表现稍好一点，因为现在能看见它，而且它有漂亮的箱体。所以他们给了稍高的分，但即便如此，他们仍觉得它比不上 Harman 的产品。

cues.en: So, you know, we get different opinions when you see the product, when you don't see the product. Another fact is that the room matters, especially at low frequencies, it matters a huge amount. Where you put the loudspeaker in the room and where you sit in the room changes what you hear. And so if you move the speakers around and do the test, we should get different opinions when the speakers are in different places. Here on the left you see the black speaker.
cues.zh: 所以你看，看得见产品和看不见产品，我们会得到不同的意见。另一个事实是房间很重要，尤其在低频，影响巨大。音箱在房间里的位置以及你坐的位置，会改变你听到的声音。所以如果移动音箱再做测试，音箱放在不同位置时，我们应该会得到不同意见。左边这里你看到的是黑色音箱。

cues.en: In the blind tests, in two locations, you get two very different ratings. Huge difference. The white speaker, same speaker, two different locations, different ratings. This one, same speaker, different locations, different ratings. Same speaker, different locations, different ratings. You let them see the speakers, and suddenly those differences disappear. They say, well, it's the same speaker. It has to sound the same. I gave it a 5.6 the first time, I'll give it a 5.6 the second time.
cues.zh: 在盲测中，两个位置会得到两个非常不同的评分。差异巨大。白色音箱，同一只音箱，两个不同位置，评分不同。这一只，同一只音箱，不同位置，评分不同。同一只音箱，不同位置，评分不同。可你让他们看见音箱，这些差异突然就消失了。他们会说，嗯，这是同一只音箱，听起来肯定一样。我第一次给 5.6，第二次还给 5.6。

cues.en: They just kind of go deaf. Different recordings matter. I mean, recordings are not spectrally balanced in the same way. They don't have the same instrumental content. And so they will reveal problems in loudspeakers in different ways. And that's why we use a bunch of different recordings. And here we have in the blind tests, the black lines showing that the choice of recording affected the average preference rating.
cues.zh: 他们就像突然聋了一样。不同录音也很重要。我的意思是，录音的频谱平衡并不相同，器乐内容也不一样。所以它们会以不同方式暴露音箱的问题。这就是为什么我们要用一堆不同的录音。这里在盲测中，黑线显示录音的选择影响了平均偏好评分。

cues.en: But in the sighted test, didn't make a difference. Play me anything. I'll give you the same number. It's interesting. And experience makes listeners fussier. And this has gone on for years. We noticed this a long time ago that the people who are involved with the program and do a lot of critical listening, they're not as easily impressed as people without that kind of...
cues.zh: 但在非盲测中，这没有造成差异。随便放什么给我听，我都给你同一个分数。这很有意思。而且经验会让听者更挑剔。这种情况已经持续多年。我们很久以前就注意到，参与这个项目、做大量批判性听音的人，不像没有那种……

cues.en: background experience. And so the scores from the inexperienced listeners go up, and you'll see that the males and the females agree. So if anybody who has, entertains notions of sexism, you can forget them. And this is not the first time I've done this kind of test. The listeners of both sexes are just fine, except that more males suffer from hearing loss than females. And so there's the probability that you'll have some faulty opinions from people, from males with hearing loss.
cues.zh: 背景经验的人那么容易被打动。于是，没经验听者的评分会更高，而且你会看到男性和女性意见一致。所以如果有人抱有性别歧视的念头，可以打消了。这不是我第一次做这种测试。两种性别的听者都没问题，只不过男性患听力损失的比例比女性高。所以有可能出现一些有问题的意见，来自有听力损失的男性。

cues.en: We just enjoyed louder hobbies, I guess. So when you do sighted evaluations, when you know what you're listening to, even if you can't lay eyes on it, if you just know what you're listening to, your opinions are biased, even before the first note of music has been played. If you believe something, you very likely will hear it.
cues.zh: 我们大概只是更喜欢声音更大的爱好。所以，当你进行明察评测时，当你知道自己在听什么时，即使你看不到它，只要你知道自己在听什么，你的观点就已经带有偏见了，甚至在音乐的第一个音符响起之前就是如此。如果你相信某件事，你很可能真的会“听见”它。

cues.en: And this happens, you know, those, anybody here is an audio file or reads the audio file press will know immediately what I'm saying. I mean, this is why these are the imagined, not real, imagined differences between speaker wires and that kind of thing. They're not real. They are, it's complete marketing. Is the room a fundamental problem? Well, I...
cues.zh: 而且这种情况确实会发生。这里如果有人是发烧友，或者读过音频类媒体的文章，肯定马上就明白我在说什么。我的意思是，这就是为什么人们会臆想出音箱线之类东西之间的差异，而这些差异并不真实。它们完全是营销手段。房间是一个根本性问题吗？嗯，我……

cues.en: One of the last things that was done before I left was to prepare this experiment, and it was done after I left, where we compared three really good loudspeakers. They were closely rated. The differences were subtle. You had to pay attention to make the test a difficult test. And so we compared these three loudspeakers in three different rooms, completely blind. There was a screen. The listeners couldn't see what they were hearing.
cues.zh: 我离开前完成的最后几件事之一，就是准备这个实验。实验是在我离开之后进行的：我们比较了三款真正出色的扬声器。它们的评分非常接近，差异很细微。你必须集中注意力，才能让这项测试变得困难。因此，我们在三个不同的房间里，对这三款扬声器进行了完全盲测。现场有一块屏幕，听众看不到自己听到的是什么。

cues.en: And we randomized the positions and did it several times. It was all then properly balanced from a scientific point of view. And the upshot of it was that in each of these three very different rooms, the listeners were able to rate the loudspeakers and they rated them in almost precisely the same way, certainly the same order. The numbers changed a little bit, but only a little bit. It's remarkable how small the differences were when you think of how large the acoustical,
cues.zh: 我们还随机安排扬声器的位置，并重复进行了多次。从科学角度看，整个实验经过了适当的平衡。结果是，在这三个截然不同的房间里，听众都能给扬声器评分，而且评分方式几乎完全一致，至少顺序肯定相同。分数会有一点变化，但只有一点点。想想这些房间的声学特性差异有多大，就会发现结果多么令人惊讶，

cues.en: The sound feels different from one another. Greatly different from one another. So we conclude that we have some ability to listen through rooms. It happens in live performances. We don't have to equalize a Steinway or a Bozendorfer piano for which the room it's in. It's the loudspeaker or it's the piano or whatever it is in the room.
cues.zh: 然而声音听起来却彼此不同，差异非常大。所以我们得出结论：人确实有能力透过房间去聆听。在现场演出中也是如此。我们不需要因为Steinway或Boesendorfer钢琴所在的房间不同，就对它们进行均衡。真正发声的是扬声器，或者钢琴，或者房间里的其他声源。

cues.en: and we can separate the sound of the piano or the voice or whatever it is from the room to a great extent. And when you think about what's going on, what has to be going on in this brain between our two ears, it's a remarkable thing because based on masses at 40 years of doing this, I can say that in order to give me or us, anybody, any experimenter, consistent
cues.zh: 我们在很大程度上能够把钢琴、声音或其他声源的声音，与房间的声音区分开来。想想我们两耳之间的大脑究竟在做什么，这真是一件不可思议的事。因为基于我从事这项工作四十多年的大量经验，我可以说，为了让我、让我们，或者让任何实验者，持续稳定地听到

cues.en: the sounds that these people are hearing, they will have had to do these things. They will have had to extract from the sound field the timbral contribution from the loudspeaker so that they can comment on the loudspeaker. And to do that, they have to separate the loudspeaker's timbral signature from the room. And in order to make sense of either of those,
cues.zh: 这些人所听到的声音，他们一定做了下面这些事。他们必须从声场中提取出扬声器的音色贡献，这样才能评价扬声器。要做到这一点，他们必须把扬声器的音色特征与房间的影响区分开来。而为了理解其中任何一者，

cues.en: they will have had to take into account the timbral signature of the program, the recording. And believe me, nobody could ever claim to have been at the final mix of the recording they're listening to. So how on earth is this possible? How can people, even inexperienced people, do this? How can experienced people do this? This is one heck of a party Turk.
cues.zh: 他们还必须考虑节目的音色特征，也就是录音本身的音色。相信我，没人能声称自己曾亲自参与过正在聆听的那份录音的最终混音。那么，这一切究竟是怎么可能的？即使是没有经验的人，怎么做到的？有经验的人又是怎么做到的？这简直是一项绝活。

cues.en: Really and truly. And in the end, after pondering this for years, it has to be, you know, Bregman, another McGill alumni, his auditory scene analysis, it has to be that we are streaming in our minds, we are separately streaming the sound of the musical instrument or the loudspeaker reproducing that musical instrument from the room
cues.zh: 确实是这样。琢磨了这么多年之后，最终答案必然是——就像另一位 McGill 校友 Bregman 的听觉场景分析所指出的——我们的大脑在进行声音分流，把乐器（或播放乐器的扬声器）的声音与房间本身的声音分开了。

cues.en: They're separate. If you go to a concert and the bass is weak, you don't blame the bass instrument or the musician playing the bass instrument. You blame the concert hall. So we are able to do that, and we do it just subconsciously. If my voice has a sudden tandral richness, you may recognize that we're in the men's room.
cues.zh: 两者是分开的。如果你去听音乐会发现低音很弱，你不会怪低音乐器或乐手，而是会怪音乐厅。所以我们完全有这种能力，而且是下意识做到的。如果我的声音突然变得共鸣丰富，你可能就会意识到我们是在男洗手间里。

cues.en: It's because of the reverberation in the room. It's still me on a scale of 10. The fidelity rating for my voice is going to be 10. But it's just Floyd in this room as opposed to Floyd in a different room. So we seem to do this, and this is an amazing feat. Okay, we can do this. We can actually listen to loudspeakers in rooms and offer up opinions on those loudspeakers that are repeatable.
cues.zh: 这是因为房间里的混响。以满分10分来看，那依然是我，对我声音的保真度评分依然会是10分。只不过是这个房间里的 Floyd，而不是另一个房间里的 Floyd。我们似乎确实具备这种能力，这真是一项了不起的本领。好了，既然我们能做到，我们就能在房间里实际试听扬声器，并给出具有可复现性的评价，

cues.en: from person to person, from time to time, and for different kinds of program material. So we have a growing database of subjective measurements. Now we're going to create a parallel database of technical measurements so that we can start to stand back and compare one to the other and hopefully figure out what it is in the technical performance of loudspeakers that makes some appealing
cues.zh: 无论因人而异、因时而异，还是面对不同的节目素材。因此我们积累了一个不断扩大的主观测试数据库。现在我们要建立一个平行的客观技术测试数据库，这样就能抽身出来将二者进行对比，希望能找出扬声器的哪些技术指标让某些扬声器深受大众喜爱，

cues.en: to people at large and others that are not. We have to admit right away that there is no single curve, no frequency response curve or whatever curve you choose to identify it as, that can completely describe the performance of a loudspeaker. It radiates sound in all directions into a somewhat reflective space, a room. And the sound field, by the time it gets to the listener,
cues.zh: 而另一些则不然。我们必须立刻承认，没有任何一条单一曲线——无论是频率响应曲线还是其他任何曲线——能够完整描述扬声器的性能。它是向所有方向辐射声音到具有一定反射性的空间（也就是房间）中。而当声场到达听众时，

cues.en: It's extremely complicated. There's no way to unravel that complex structure. You can't just put a microphone at the listening location and somehow analyze what it picks up and go back to figure out from that what the loudspeaker sent out. It's impossible. You can't go backwards. You can go forwards though. You can measure the sound that leaves the loudspeaker.
cues.zh: 它已经极其复杂了。根本无法解构这种复杂的结构。你不能只是在聆听位置放一个麦克风，分析它采集到的声音，然后反向推导出扬声器最初发出了什么。这是不可能的，你无法逆向反推。但你可以正向测量：你可以测量从扬声器发出的声音，

cues.en: in all manner of different directions and surmise from those measurements what would arrive at a listener's location in a room. So here's what we do. We do the spinorama that Viaslav mentioned. It's 70 measurements at two meters in an anechoic chamber. We spin the speaker horizontally and then lay it on its side and spin it, get a vertical orbit. 70 measurements to measure the frequency response.
cues.zh: 朝向所有不同方向的声音，并根据这些测量推断出房间内到达听众位置的声音。所以我们的做法是：采用 Viaslav 提到的 Spinorama 测量法。这是在消声室中、相距两米进行的70次测量。我们水平旋转扬声器，然后将其侧放再旋转，获得垂直轨迹。通过这70次测量来测定频率响应。

cues.en: In those 70 measurements, we look at the direct sound, the on axis. It's the first sound to arrive at the listener in the sweet spot. But we tend to want these days to entertain more than one person, so we do a measurement called the listening window, which is plus or minus 30 degrees, plus or minus 10 degrees, thus accommodating a reasonable audience, frankly. It works at home, it works even here.
cues.zh: 在这70项测量中，我们看直达声，也就是轴向声。它是听音位上的听众最先听到的声音。但如今我们往往想款待不止一个人，所以我们做一项叫聆听窗口的测量，即正负30度、正负10度，坦白说，这样能容纳合理的听众范围。它在家有用，甚至在这里也有用。

cues.en: We measure early reflected sounds because sounds off the floor, the side walls and the ceiling are the strongest, the second loudest sound you hear in a room are the first reflections. So it's probably wise to pay attention to those. And to do that, what we do is we know the angle that communicates that wall bounce to the listening area, that wall bounce to the listening area, the ceiling and so on. So you measure those off-axis angles.
cues.zh: 我们测量早期反射声，因为来自地板、侧墙和天花板的反射最强，房间里听到的第二响亮的声音就是首次反射。所以关注这些大概很明智。要做到这点，我们知道墙面反射到听音区的角度，侧墙反射到听音区、天花板等等。所以测量那些离轴角度。

cues.en: and put those into the equations. And to get the late reflections, everything else, you just do the sound power, which is the sound radiated in all directions indiscriminately. Just add it all up. And the computer will chew away for a nanosecond at that data set and spit out a family of curves like this. The on axis is the solid top line. Then there's the listening window. And ideally, you want the listening window to be
cues.zh: 并把它们代入公式。而要得到后期反射，也就是其余所有，只需计算声功率，即不加区分地向所有方向辐射的声。全部加起来。计算机会瞬间处理那组数据，吐出一组像这样的曲线。轴向是顶部实线。然后是聆听窗口。理想情况下，你希望聆听窗口

cues.en: as nearly identical as possible to the on axis, so that the person in the sweet spot and the people adjacent get the same kind of direct sound, because the first sound to arrive carries with it the central timbral signature of the voice of the musical instrument. And then we were interested to see if the follow-up sounds match that timbral signature, the reflections from the rest of the room, whether those...
cues.zh: 尽可能接近轴向，这样最佳听音位上的人和旁边的人得到同类的直达声，因为最先到达的声音带有乐器声音的核心音色特征。然后我们感兴趣的是后续声音是否匹配那个音色特征，即房间其余部分的反射，那些是否……

cues.en: are communicating similar temporal cues to our ears, so we look at the early reflected sounds. This is the energy sum of the floor-ceaning side wall balances and back and front wall balances. Then we add up, in a weighted sense, it's a complicated calculation, but we actually compute the estimated sound power radiated from the loudspeaker without regard to direction. We then compute two more numbers.
cues.zh: 是否向我们的耳朵传达相似的时间线索，所以我们看早期反射声。这是地板-天花板、侧墙以及后墙和前墙反射的能量总和。然后我们按加权方式相加，计算很复杂，但我们实际计算的是扬声器不分方向辐射的估计声功率。然后我们再算两个数。

cues.en: the directivity index of zero would be an omnidirectional source, sound radiated equally in all directions. And that is the case with all woofers and subwoofers. Once the sound source is small compared to the wavelength that radiates, it radiates equally in all directions. And so the wavelength at 20 hertz is...
cues.zh: 指向性指数为零意味着全指向声源，声音向所有方向均匀辐射。所有低音单元和超低音单元都是如此。一旦声源相对于辐射波长很小，它就会向所有方向均匀辐射。所以20赫兹的波长是……

cues.en: 57 feet, 100 hertz is 11.3 feet, and the woofer is only a foot. So no, even at 100 hertz, the woofers are essentially omnidirectional. They don't care which way you point them. And so we calculate these rectivity indexes as a function of frequency, and they are really telling us something about the uniformity with which the loudspeaker radiates its energy into the room.
cues.zh: 57英尺，100赫兹是11.3英尺，而低音单元只有一英尺。所以不对，即使在100赫兹，低音单元基本上也是全指向的。它们不在乎你指向哪个方向。于是我们计算这些指向性指数随频率的变化，它们实际上告诉我们扬声器向房间辐射能量的均匀程度。

cues.en: At low frequencies, it's omnidirectional. And as you go up in frequency, it becomes more and more progressively directional facing the audience. And then at high frequencies, it will be quite narrow. What we want is a loudspeaker that maintains something resembling a constant directivity over a wide range of frequencies. In that way and only in that way will we achieve this ideal performance of the direct sound.
cues.zh: 低频时，它是全向的。随着频率升高，它越来越指向听众。到了高频，它会变得相当窄。我们想要的是这样一种扬声器：在很宽的频率范围内保持类似恒定指向性。只有这样，也只有这样，我们才能实现直达声的理想表现。

cues.en: matching the timbre of the reflected cells. This spinorama, by the way, is now embodied in a standard, published in 2013. And we'll see if anybody uses it. There are two problems with it. It's difficult to measure. Not every manufacturer has that capability.
cues.zh: 使反射声的音色相匹配。顺便说，这个 spinorama 现在已经纳入2013年发布的一项标准。我们看看有没有人用。它有两个问题。测量很难。不是每个厂商都有这个能力。

cues.en: And even if they go outside of their own premises and hire a third party to do the measurements, which they could do, they might not like what they see. And so if they don't like what they see, you're not going to see it. That's really the fact of it. So it's a challenge. But the data, if you can find this data, it's useful. Here's an example from my old original work on 1985 published in 1986.
cues.zh: 而且即使他们走出自己的场地，雇第三方来做测量——他们本可以这么做——他们也可能不喜欢看到的结果。所以，如果他们不喜欢看到的结果，你就不会看到它。事实就是这样。所以这是个挑战。但数据，如果你能找到这些数据，它是有用的。这是我1985年早期原创工作的一个例子，发表于1986年。

cues.en: Here's a loud speaker that had some directivity problems. It was designed, I know the designers, and I know the history of it. It was designed by a group of engineers who were smart, who were told to get the flattest, smoothest on-axis response they could possibly get. And that was the only instruction they were given. And they did it. They went out, I'm sure, to the local pub and had a few beers to celebrate.
cues.zh: 这是一款有指向性问题的扬声器。它被设计出来——我认识设计者，也知道它的历史。它由一群聪明的工程师设计，他们被告知要做出尽可能平坦、平滑的轴向响应。这就是他们得到的唯一指示。他们做到了。我确信，他们当时还去当地酒吧喝了几杯啤酒庆祝。

cues.en: when they did it. But what they ignored, because they weren't told to pay any attention to it, was what happens off axis. So you get this pristine first sound arriving at the sweet spot, but 60, 30, 60 degrees off axis, not so, not so good. So what does this mean in terms of how it sounds? Well, in terms of how it sounds, I can tell you that when we put this one into a double blind listening test, it didn't win and it didn't lose. It was a good solid
cues.zh: 在他们做到之后。但他们忽略的是——因为没人告诉他们要关注这一点——离轴会发生什么。所以，到达最佳听音位的直达声很纯净，但在偏轴60度、30度、60度处，就不那么，不那么好了。那么这在听感上意味着什么？就听感而言，我可以告诉你，当我们把它放进双盲听音测试时，它没赢也没输。它是一款扎实的

cues.en: mediocre loudspeaker, which it was an expensive high-end loudspeaker. It was a Kef 105.2, for those of you who might have gray hairs and can remember, which was highly regarded at the time. So here is the direct sound that arrives from that loudspeaker at a listener. That's the energy sum of the first four reflections, only the first four reflections, four ceiling sidewalls.
cues.zh: 平庸的扬声器，而它其实是一款昂贵的高端扬声器。它是 Kef 105.2，你们中那些头发花白、还记得的人可能知道，当时它评价很高。那么，这就是从那只扬声器到达听者的直达声。那是前四次反射的能量总和，只算前四次反射，四个来自天花板和侧墙的反射。

cues.en: And already we can see in the measurements why that loudspeaker had a personality, why it wasn't neutral, why it just sounded not quite right. We didn't give it our highest rating. We didn't give it our lowest rating because there are worse loudspeakers than that. But it's not perfect by any means. And when you go to the sound power, the total sound radiated in all directions, you get that. And you can see that in the total sound power and in the early reflections,
cues.zh: 从测量中我们已经能看出，为什么那只扬声器有个性，为什么它不中性，为什么它听起来就是不太对。我们没给它最高评分。也没给它最低评分，因为还有比它更差的扬声器。但它绝不算完美。再看声功率，也就是向所有方向辐射的总声，你会得到这个结果。你能在总声功率和早期反射中看到它，

cues.en: Inferior off-axis performance is the dominating factor. The fact that it's beautifully smooth and flat on axis is not a factor at all. In fact, you think about this, you look at that set of data and you ask the question, if we are to look at a data set and try to predict how a loudspeaker will sound in a room, what do we have to measure? Well, at low frequencies, we're gonna measure sound power. That's 10 dB higher than anything else.
cues.zh: 较差的离轴表现是主导因素。轴向响应漂亮、平滑、平坦这件事根本不算因素。事实上，你想想，看看那组数据并问一个问题：如果我们要看一组数据，预测扬声器在房间里听起来如何，我们必须测量什么？低频时，我们要测声功率。它比其他任何东西都高10 dB。

cues.en: At highest frequencies we can rely on the on-axis because everything else has been attenuated. The on-axis is the dominant factor at high frequencies because the tweeters are directional and the room is absorptive and air is absorptive. But once you get below about 10 kilohertz, everything gets into the act. You can ignore absolutely nothing and the on-axis response is not the dominant factor. So let's add those up and we get a room curve.
cues.zh: 在最高频段，我们可以依赖轴上响应，因为其他部分都已经衰减了。高频时轴上响应是主导因素，因为高音单元具有指向性，而房间和空气都会吸收声音。但一旦低于大约 10 千赫，所有因素都会参与进来。你完全不能忽略任何因素，轴上响应也不再是主导因素。把这些加起来，我们就得到了房间曲线。

cues.en: Now what we see in that predicted room curve is evidence that as a function of time something is happening. The direct sound, the first sound to arrive at your ears will be this black curve right here, the black one. But as a function of time, as those reflected sounds arrive at your ears, they're going to add up to that red curve at the top, the prediction.
cues.zh: 现在，从这条预测的房间曲线中可以看出，随着时间变化，确实有某些事情正在发生。直达声，也就是最先到达你耳朵的声音，会对应这里的黑色曲线，就是这条黑线。但随着时间推移，反射声陆续到达你的耳朵，它们会叠加成上方那条红色曲线，也就是预测结果。

cues.en: So now we see that what we measure in a room is dominated by the off-axis performance of the loudspeaker and the room itself, because the room has to communicate that energy to us. And if it doesn't communicate that energy equally at all frequencies, it can't be neutral. So we have two issues here. That's an interesting test. Let's just see how that prediction works. So we put that loudspeaker into a listening arm.
cues.zh: 所以现在我们看到，在房间里测得的结果，主要由扬声器的离轴性能和房间本身决定，因为房间必须把这些能量传递给我们。如果它不能在所有频率上等量传递这些能量，声音就不可能中性。因此这里有两个问题。这是个有意思的测试。我们来看看这个预测是否有效。现在把这只扬声器放到听音臂上。

cues.en: Put it down in a typical stereo left location, measure it. It's averaged over those six seats. Averaged over the six seats. Move it. We only moved it half a meter, 18 inches. Not very far. But look at the difference in the curves. Wow. You either had a kick drum that's a little fat or a kick drum that was almost absent. It's not subtle. That's what standing waves in a room do at low frequencies.
cues.zh: 把它放在典型的立体声左声道位置，进行测量。结果是六个座位的平均值。对六个座位取平均。移动它。我们只移动了半米，也就是 18 英寸，并不远。但看看曲线的差异。哇。你听到的底鼓，要么有点肥厚，要么几乎完全消失。这一点都不细微。这就是房间中的驻波在低频下造成的影响。

cues.en: And if you play around with the positions, you can find another position that looks pretty good. And if you listen while you're doing all of this, you find, yeah, that's the one that actually sounds like a pretty tight, good kick drum. I like that. Bass notes are all there. And there's our prediction. So what do we conclude? Well, first of all, the prediction worked. Not at all frequencies, but above 300 or 400 hertz, I'd say, hmm, we nailed it.
cues.zh: 如果调整摆位，你还能找到另一个看起来相当不错的位置。如果在调整过程中同时试听，你会发现，没错，这个位置的底鼓听起来确实紧实、出色。我喜欢这个效果。低音音符都清晰可见。这就是我们的预测。那么我们得出什么结论？首先，预测是有效的。虽然不是在所有频率上，但在 300 或 400 赫兹以上，我会说：嗯，预测得非常准。

cues.en: So there's enough information in the anechoic data of that loudspeaker to be able to predict what's happening in a room above 300 or 400 Hertz. What happens at lower frequencies? Well, those are the very familiar room resonances, the standing waves, the modes, the eigenmodes, people have many names for them. They're the corruption of the base in all small rooms of any shape.
cues.zh: 也就是说，这只扬声器的无响室数据包含了足够的信息，可以预测它在 300 或 400 赫兹以上的房间内表现。那更低频率会怎样？那就是我们非常熟悉的房间共振、驻波、模态和本征模，人们对它们有很多不同的称呼。它们会破坏所有小房间中的低音，而且不论房间形状如何，都会如此。

cues.en: There is no escape from them, so you have to deal with them, and I'll, if I have time, I'll show you how. So the prediction of that room curve is that it tells us that the shape of the room curve, and I'd have to say, probably, what we hear, substantially, is dictated by what happens off-axis. It's reflected energy. The only way to get rid of that reflected energy is to listen outdoors or in a very anechoic room.
cues.zh: 你无法逃避它们，所以必须设法处理。我如果有时间，会演示给你看。这个房间曲线的预测告诉我们，房间曲线的形状，以及我想很大程度上我们实际听到的声音，取决于离轴方向发生了什么，也就是反射能量。消除反射能量的唯一办法，就是在室外聆听，或者在非常理想的无响室中聆听。

cues.en: neither of which is very pleasant for listening to music, right? Rooms are good for music, even good rooms for loudspeaker reproduction of music. And in this case, if you do a room measurement and see that red curve up there, and you reach for your trusty equalizer and smooth it out, what you've done is you've screwed up the only good thing that speaker had, which was its on-axis response. You have not solved the problem.
cues.zh: 这两种听起来都不怎么舒服，对吧？房间其实适合听音乐，即便是用音箱重放音乐的优质房间也是如此。在这种情况下，如果你做了一次房间测量，看到上面的那条红线，然后拿起你信赖的均衡器把它拉平，那你其实是彻底毁掉了这台音箱唯一的优点——它的轴向响应。你并没有解决问题。

cues.en: You can't solve that problem with an equalizer. The only solution for that problem is a loudspeaker that behaves itself. So you take that one back to the shop and buy a better loudspeaker. Like that one. That's a better loudspeaker. Smooth on axis and quite well behaved off axis. And that's not a bad, the directivity index is, you know, it's not perfect, but it's not horrendous. You may put it in a room and you measure six seat average, you get that.
cues.zh: 均衡器根本解决不了这个问题。唯一的办法就是换一台自身表现合格的音箱。所以你得把那个退回店里，换个更好的音箱。比如那台，那才算个好音箱。轴向平滑，离轴表现也非常规整。而且还不赖，指向性指数嘛，虽然谈不上完美，但绝不算差。把它放进房间里测量六个座位的平均值，就会得到那个结果。

cues.en: Now there's the sound power and the inverse of the directivity index, if you turn the directivity index upside down, you will get an estimate of the sound power if that loudspeaker is equalized to be perfectly flat or created to be perfectly flat on axis. Now this one was almost perfectly flat on axis to begin with. And so the inverse of the directivity index and the sound power that we actually measured
cues.zh: 现在来看声功率和指向性指数的倒数。如果把指向性指数上下颠倒过来，只要音箱经过均衡后轴向完全平直，或者出厂时轴向就非常平直，你就能据此估算出它的声功率。而这台音箱一开始的轴向响应就几乎完全平直。因此，指向性指数的倒数和我们实际测得的声功率……

cues.en: sit one on top of the other, and if we move them down, they give us a pretty good picture of the room curve above 200 hertz. Only when you get up into the above seven or eight kilohertz does the tweeter start to dominate, and the sound power curve doesn't weight the tweeter output sufficiently, so we have to add some more information, but I can tell you that what we're seeing is that
cues.zh: 几乎完全重叠。如果我们把它们向下平移，就能非常清晰地展现出 200 赫兹以上的房间曲线。只有升到七八千赫兹以上时，高音单元才开始占主导地位，而声功率曲线对高音单元输出的加权并不充分，所以我们还得补充一些信息，但我可以明确告诉大家：

cues.en: over most of the critical part of the frequency range, we can predict a room curve from the anechoic measurements. It's not a mystery. There's another one. Now, this is not a perfect loudspeaker. This is a modern version of what I just showed you. In fact, I heard a pair of those today. They're here. And the on axis is not flat and smooth, and the off axis certainly isn't flat and smooth. The directivity index is not smooth.
cues.zh: 在绝大多数关键频段内，我们完全可以通过消声室的测量结果来预测房间曲线。这其实毫无悬念。再看另一个例子。这台可不是什么完美的音箱，它是我刚才展示的那款的现代版本。其实我今天还听了一对，就在现场。它的轴向不平滑，离轴表现显然也不平滑，指向性指数同样不平滑。

cues.en: But because the on axis is not smooth, then we will see that these curves are not the same. And let's just see that sound power now should be the best predictor of the room curve, and by golly it is. And so then the inverse of the directivity index is not bad. If you had nothing else to work with, it would be pretty good. All I'm hoping I'm developing in your minds is the idea that these cold scientific...
cues.zh: 正因为轴向不平滑，我们就会发现这些曲线并不一致。大家再看，声功率现在应该成了房间曲线的最佳预测指标，天哪，果真如此。这样一来指向性指数的倒数也还过得去。如果你手头没有别的数据可用，拿它顶上倒也挺不错。我只希望让大家心里形成一个概念：这些看似冰冷的科学……

cues.en: numbers and graphs that we measure in our anechoic chambers are quite relevant to what we hear in rooms. They're not abstract. Now that loudspeaker has two problems. It's not flat on axis and an equalizer can fix that because an equalizer just changes the amplitude response, the frequency response. But it has problematic directivity and an equalizer cannot fix that.
cues.zh: 我们在消声室里测量的数字和曲线，与我们在房间里听到的声音密切相关。它们不是抽象的。现在，这个扬声器有两个问题。它的轴上响应不平坦，而均衡器可以解决这个问题，因为均衡器只会改变幅度响应，也就是频率响应。但它的指向性有问题，均衡器解决不了。

cues.en: and both of those contribute to the fact that the room curve is not flat. If you don't know that top data about the loudspeaker and all you do is measure the room curve, which most people do, a lot of receivers will do this automatically for you. You press the button and it makes funny sounds and reassures you that it has calibrated your loudspeaker and room combination. Well, that's what it's measuring and it has no idea.
cues.zh: 这两点共同导致房间曲线不平坦。如果你不了解扬声器的上述数据，只测量房间曲线，而大多数人确实这么做，很多接收机还会自动替你完成。你按下按钮，它就播放一些奇怪的声音，让你以为它已经校准好了扬声器和房间的组合。实际上，它测到的就是这些，而它根本不知道问题出在哪里。

cues.en: What's wrong with the loudspeaker or what's wrong with the room? It doesn't know what's causing it, so it doesn't know what to do to correct it. In this case, equalization is not going to solve the problem. Only a better loudspeaker will. Now, these are popular terms. I don't know. Does anybody here have a room equalizer in their home system or business system? Yeah, it had to be one. Thank you.
cues.zh: 是扬声器有问题，还是房间有问题？它不知道是什么导致了问题，也就不知道该如何修正。在这种情况下，均衡并不能解决问题，只有更好的扬声器才行。现在，这些都是很流行的说法。我不清楚。在座有人在家用音响系统或商用系统里使用房间均衡器吗？有，肯定有一个。谢谢。

cues.en: No, because if you go to your local, if you order it by any of the modern day domestic surround receivers, many of them have these algorithms built into them. You can go out and spend hundreds or a thousand or more dollars for a standalone device box that does this for you, or you can pay somebody to come in and do it for you. It's a system, it's a service.
cues.zh: 不，因为如果你去本地商店，或者订购如今的家用环绕声接收机，很多设备都内置了这些算法。你可以花几百美元，甚至一千多美元，买一个独立的设备来替你完成这件事，也可以花钱请人上门替你做。这是一套系统，也是一项服务。

cues.en: And the claim is that by making such measurements on unknown loudspeakers in unknown rooms, that we can create perfection for anybody anywhere. And unfortunately, there are some standards from SMPTE, this is the motion picture industry, ISO, ITU, that actually promote this belief. And I'm afraid to say it is simply not true. It can't be true, and it isn't true. And in my dying years,
cues.zh: 他们声称，只要对未知扬声器和未知房间进行这样的测量，就能为任何人在任何地方创造完美效果。遗憾的是，SMPTE，也就是电影行业，ISO 和 ITU 都有一些标准，实际上在推动这种观点。恐怕我得说，这根本不是真的。不可能是真的，事实也确实不是这样。在我的晚年，

cues.en: I'm going to do my damnedest to change it. And the fact is that when you consider all of the audible characteristics that two ears in the brain can extract from the sound field of sound source in a room, it's not going to be accurately represented by a microphone and a simple analyzer. It's just, it's a presumption that isn't true. What we're measuring is not what we're hearing. So back to now what we are measuring.
cues.zh: 我会竭尽全力改变这种状况。事实上，当你考虑到双耳和大脑能够从房间内声源的声场中提取出的所有可听特征时，这些特征不可能被一个麦克风和一个简单的分析器准确表示出来。这只是一个并不成立的假设。我们测量到的，并不是我们听到的。那么，现在回到我们实际测量的内容。

cues.en: And what we are measuring is that the loudspeaker is in control over part of the frequency range. The room is in control over part of the frequency range. And the transition frequency between the room and the loudspeaker control varies with the size of the room. And as the room gets larger, the loudspeaker takes over more and more control. So in a room this size, the loudspeaker is going to be in control down to probably
cues.zh: 我们测量到的是，在部分频率范围内，扬声器起主导作用；在另一部分频率范围内，房间起主导作用。房间和扬声器之间的过渡频率会随房间大小而变化。房间越大，扬声器所控制的范围就越大。所以在这么大的房间里，扬声器大概会一直控制到

cues.en: to go 40, 50 Hertz. And below that we're gonna have to pay some attention to this particular space. But above that, we have some assurance that what you're going to hear will be dominantly influenced by the loudspeaker. And so, in theory, if I'm right, all I need to do is to put a really good loudspeaker here, turn it on, and you'll be a happy camper.
cues.zh: 40、50 赫兹左右。低于这个频率，我们就得特别关注这个空间。但在此之上，我们可以确信，你听到的声音主要会受到扬声器的影响。所以理论上，如果我的判断没错，我只需要在这里放一个真正优秀的扬声器，打开它，你们就会很满意。

cues.en: except at low frequencies. We may have to pay some attention to low frequencies. Now, the interesting thing is that I was thinking along these lines, and then I stumbled into a man named Art Benéde, a physicist, musician, brilliant man. He's dead now, but here he died. He sent to me a collection of his writings, and this was among them. I said, well, this is it, because he just said, well, look, as a musician, it's obvious.
cues.zh: 除非在低频段。我们可能得对低频多加注意。有意思的是，我当时正顺着这个思路想，偶然遇到了一位叫 Art Benéde 的人，他是物理学家兼音乐家，才华横溢。他现在已经去世了，但在去世前寄给我一本他的文集，这就是其中一篇。我说，没错就是这个，因为他说，你看，作为一个音乐家，这显而易见。

cues.en: The musical source is well defined. I mean, I can play the same riff 10 times, and it'll be the same acoustical output 10 times. And back in the audience, it sounds the same 10 times. But if you make measurements, and you walk around the audience, and it still sounds the same, but if you make measurements from here to there, it's going to be very different. You put the microphone in different positions, you find huge, huge, huge variations. He's suggesting...
cues.zh: 声源是明确定义的。我是说，同一段乐句我可以弹 10 遍，10 次的声学输出都是一样的。而在台下听来，这 10 次听上去也是一样的。但如果你去测量——你在观众席走动，听起来依然一样，但要是把不同位置的数据做对比，结果就会大不相同。把麦克风放在不同位置，你会发现极大的差异。他的意思是……

cues.en: or my interpretation of his suggestion is that if we were able to describe the sound source in measurements, then we should be able to predict what listeners are hearing. What happens in between maybe doesn't matter quite so much because they're going to be very, very difficult to interpret. I mean, if you make measurements in a concert hall, put a sound source on the stage and measure back in the audience and...
cues.zh: 或者说我对他的观点的理解是，如果我们能通过测量来描述声源，就应该能够预测听众听到的是什么。中间发生的过程或许没那么重要，因为那些数据极其难以解读。我是说，如果你在音乐厅里测量，把声源放在舞台上，然后在观众席测量……

cues.en: do a frequency response, transfer function, what have you. It's going to be awful, awful, awful, awful. An engineer will look at it and say, this is just a staggeringly complicated comb filter. Can't possibly sound good. Communication may be impossible. And yet we go there and we listen to it and we love it. It's a reference listening experience. That's the difference between what we are measuring and what we are hearing. And in this case, we are measuring the wrong thing.
cues.zh: 测个频率响应、传递函数等等。结果会极其糟糕。工程师一看会说，这简直就是个复杂得惊人的梳状滤波器。声音根本不可能好听，甚至连信息传递都成问题。但我们去现场听，却非常喜欢，那是一种参考级的听音体验。这就是我们测量的和我们听到的之间的差距。而在这种情况下，我们测错了东西。

cues.en: So let's just draw the parallel between live performance and reproduction. We have musical instrument, plus room to the brain. The brain sorts it all out. Now, if we have a good recording of that instrument, reproduced by a good loudspeaker, we should be able to sort of have a parallel experience in our homes. And that's the challenge. That's what we're going to see if it happens. I'll tell you it does happen, actually.
cues.zh: 所以我们把现场演奏和声音重放做个类比。乐器加上房间，传到大脑，大脑会把这一切理顺。现在，如果我们有那件乐器的优质录音，再通过优秀的扬声器重放，在家里应该也能获得类似的体验。这正是挑战所在，也是我们要验证是否可行的。其实我可以告诉你，这确实行得通。

cues.en: But the success of that whole exercise will depend on the competence of the loudspeaker designer and on the ability of the recording industry, that's you people, some of you anyway, to capture and store accurate renderings of what was the sounds that were radiated by those voices and musical instruments that we care to listen to.
cues.zh: 但这一切能否成功，取决于扬声器设计者的水平，也取决于唱片行业的能力——也就是在座的各位，至少是你们中的一部分人——能否准确捕捉并记录我们想听的那些人声与乐器所辐射出的真实声音。

cues.en: And this is an artistic exercise and you just go into any one of these control rooms and you see these massive consoles and offside apparatus with knobs and dials and all kinds of processing available and that is perfectly legitimate. But you know, it's legitimate and it's part of the problem. Not that the art shouldn't be whatever the artist wants it to be, it's just that we have trouble delivering that art to the customer.
cues.zh: 这是一种艺术实践，你随便走进一间控制室，就会看到那些巨大的调音台和旁边布满旋钮、表盘的各种处理设备，这完全合情合理。但你知道，这合情合理，却也是问题的一部分。倒不是说艺术不该随艺术家的心意，而是我们很难把这种艺术完整传递给客户。

cues.en: See, we listen in homes, in our cars, and through headphones. That's the audio industry. Audio industry is you capture sound, you process it, you send it off to a live audience in real time. You can store it, you can send it off to customers in wherever they want to press a play button. Or you can send it off to a different form of storage and send it off to the cinema world. So that's the audio industry as I know it, as I've worked in it all of my professional career.
cues.zh: 你看，我们在家里听，在车里听，用耳机听。这就是音频行业。音频行业就是：采集声音，处理声音，实时传送给现场观众；或者存储起来，送到客户想按播放键的任何地方；又或者换种介质存储，送进影院。这就是我所了解、也奉献了整个职业生涯的音频行业。

cues.en: And my philosophy is embodied in this, science in the service of art is our business. And when you combine those three words, it's kind of oxymoronic, science and art together. Yeah, what's business? Science and business, no, it doesn't work. Art and business, yeah, music, yes. But good sound is our product. I mean, I worked for a manufacturer that made boxes that cost money, wooden boxes, steel boxes.
cues.zh: 我的理念可以归结为一句话：用科学服务艺术就是我们的业务。把这三个词放一起其实挺矛盾的——科学与艺术并存。对吧，那什么是业务？科学与商业？行不通。艺术与商业？倒还可以，比如音乐。但好声音才是我们的产品。我是说，我曾为一家制造箱体的厂商工作，那些箱子价值不菲，有木质的、钢制的。

cues.en: But it's the sound that's the product. That's what puts the smile on the customer's face or the frown on the customer's face. If we screw up, the customer's not happy. And it's not happy because the box doesn't look good. He's not happy because the sound isn't good. So how do we know what good is? We listen. And when we listen, we get caught into what I call the circle of confusion, where loudspeakers are evaluated using recordings.
cues.zh: 但声音才是真正的产品。它能让客户露出笑容，也能让人皱起眉头。如果我们搞砸了，客户就会不高兴。客户不高兴不是因为箱子不好看，而是因为声音不好听。那我们怎么知道什么是“好”？靠听。而一旦去听，我们就会陷入我所谓的“混乱之环”——用录音去评估扬声器。

cues.en: And those recordings were created in control rooms where you play with microphones, select microphones, position microphones, play with equalizers, add spatial temporal effects and what have you, while you are monitoring what you're doing through loudspeakers. And so you know where this is going, right? I mean, the loudspeakers aren't standardized. Over the years, they have varied horrendously.
cues.zh: 而这些录音是在控制室里制作出来的，你在那里挑选麦克风、摆位麦克风、调试均衡器、添加时空特效等等，同时通过扬声器监听自己的操作。所以你明白问题所在了吧？扬声器根本没有统一标准。这么多年来，它们的表现差异大得惊人。

cues.en: And I've recently even been into control rooms where I wouldn't give house room to the speakers that they are listening to. They're creating art through really dreadful products, dreadful loudspeakers. And as a result, the recordings are variable.
cues.zh: 我最近甚至去过一些控制室，他们用来监听的音箱，白送给我我都嫌占地方。他们竟然通过如此糟糕的产品、如此差劲的扬声器来创作艺术。结果就是，录音品质参差不齐。

cues.en: talking to this just not long ago, saying, you know, I sat down with headphones on, which I don't normally do very much. I don't really care much for headphone listening. But in this case, I was going to explore the streaming music sources and see how they were doing for keeping sound levels, the playback levels, relatively constant from tune to tune. They do that quite well sometimes. But they also...
cues.zh: 不久前我还聊起这个，我说，你知道吗，我戴上耳机坐下来——我平时很少这样，我其实不太喜欢戴耳机听音乐。但这次，我是想测试一下流媒体音乐平台，看它们在曲目切换时能否把音量、也就是回放电平保持得相对一致。有时它们做得挺好，但同时……

cues.en: I realized immediately that the timbral balance, the spectral balance was varying hugely. So I went into the algorithm, played with the bass control, played with the treble control, and found that really quite a high percentage of the recordings I was listening to benefited from tone control adjustments. Those old fashioned things, bass and treble. My daddy's apparatus used to have...
cues.zh: 我立刻意识到音色平衡、频谱平衡差异非常大。所以我调了算法，试着调低音，试着调高音，发现我听的唱片里有相当大一部分都能从音调调节中改善听感。就是低音和高音这些老式玩意儿，当年我老爸的音响设备上就有的……

cues.en: You know, it's because they are variable. Well, why are they variable? Part of it at least has to be the monitoring circumstances because if the monitor speakers are radiating too much bass, you don't put as much bass into the disc, into the recording. And on and on it goes. You can see where this is. It's not heavy medicine here. We have to have some relationship between the domain within which the art is created and the domain within which the art is appreciated.
cues.zh: 你看，这是因为它们本身就各不相同。那为什么会有差异呢？至少有一部分原因是监听环境造成的，因为如果监听音箱低音太重，你在录音压盘时就不会放那么多低音。如此循环往复。你能看出问题在哪了，这并不是什么深奥的道理。在创造艺术的环境与欣赏艺术的环境之间，必须存在某种对应关系。

cues.en: These professional monitor loudspeakers and rooms have to behave in some ways similar to our consumer loudspeakers and rooms or cars even, or the system doesn't work. The art that is being so carefully created by the performers and by the recording engineers, that art is not being communicated to the audience in a way that allows the audience to say with any certainty that if I don't like it,
cues.zh: 这些专业监听音箱和录音室在某些方面必须表现得类似于我们的消费级音箱、普通房间甚至汽车，否则整套系统就根本行不通。表演者和录音工程师精心创作的艺术，就无法准确传递给听众，以至于听众根本无法断定，要是自己觉得不好听，

cues.en: I don't know who to blame. Do I blame my loudspeakers? Is it my room that's the problem? Or was it just a crappy recording? And that's the dilemma you're in, unless you have measurements. And so we can anticipate the sound field in a room, the physical sound field in a room from that spinorama data. The real challenge now is does that translate into what we perceive?
cues.zh: 到底该怪谁。该怪我的音箱吗？还是我房间声学环境的问题？或者纯粹是录音太烂了？除非有测量数据，否则你就会陷入这种两难。而通过 Spinorama 数据，我们就能预判房间内的声场，也就是物理声场。现在的真正挑战在于：这能否转化为我们实际感知到的听感？

cues.en: One day I got a phone call from the CEO of Harmon saying, tool, we pay you a lot of money to make sure our products sound good. Yes. Well, can you explain the recent or the current consumer reports review of loudspeakers in which some of our products did not do well? Well, I said, can I talk? So we went into his office and we talked and I explained to him that
cues.zh: 有一天我接到 Harmon 的 CEO 打来的电话，他说：“Toole，我们花大价钱雇你，是为了确保我们的产品声音好听。”“是的。”“那你能不能解释一下 Consumer Reports 最新的一期音箱评测？我们有些产品的成绩可不怎么样。”我说：“能当面聊聊吗？”于是我们去了他的办公室，我向他解释说，

cues.en: for decades, those of us in the loudspeaker business knew that Consumer Reports' reviews didn't really mean anything because they were doing it wrong. Well, he said, can we teach them to do it right? And I said, yeah, probably. It's going to take some money and some time. And so he authorized it. He just says, OK, do it. Make it so. So Sean Olive and I got together, and we put together what we knew.
cues.zh: 几十年来，我们做音箱这行的人都知道 Consumer Reports 的评测根本说明不了什么，因为他们的测试方法是错的。他说：“那我们能教会他们用正确的方法测吗？”我说：“应该可以，但这需要花些钱和时间。”于是他当场批准了，直接说：“行，去办吧，就这么定。”于是我和 Sean Olive 聚在一起，整合了我们所掌握的全部知识，

cues.en: about the psycho-acoustic relationships between these curves and numbers and subjective opinions. And we went back to our database because at Harmon we do these listening tests routinely and we do the measurements on our own products and on our competitor's products so we know where we stand. And at that particular time we had a database of 70, on 70 loudspeakers.
cues.zh: 也就是这些曲线、数据与主观评价之间的心理声学关联。我们调出了数据库，因为在 Harmon 我们会定期做这些听音测试，既测自己的产品也测竞品，所以我们很清楚自己的水准。而在那个时候，我们的数据库里已经积累了 70 款音箱的数据。

cues.en: These double-blind single-listener meticulous listening tests where the result was a score on a scale of 10. Now that's listening to a loudspeaker in a room. So that's the combination of the loudspeaker and the room that's being rated. Part two of the test is to take those loudspeakers into the anechoic chamber, do the spinorama, and process that spinorama data through an algorithm that
cues.zh: 这些双盲、单听者、细致的听力测试，结果是在10分制量表上的一个分数。注意，这是在房间里听一只扬声器。所以被评分的是扬声器和房间的组合。测试的第二部分，是把这些扬声器带进消声室，做 Spinorama，然后用一个算法处理这些 Spinorama 数据，这个算法

cues.en: tries to pay attention to spectral balance, on and off axis, bandwidth, narrow band, timbral problems, resonances, and what have you, and come up with a number. So we have a calculated number based on the Anacorte data, and we have the number that came out of the listening test, and the correlation was .86. That's not shabby. You go to Las Vegas with those odds, they'll kick you out of the casino in no time.
cues.zh: 会尽量关注轴向和离轴的频谱平衡、带宽、窄带、音色问题、共振等等，然后给出一个数值。于是我们有一个基于 Anacorte 数据的计算数值，还有一个来自听力测试的数值，相关性是0.86。这可不差。你带着这种胜算去 Las Vegas，赌场很快就会把你赶出去。

cues.en: But going back to the origin of the motivation for this, consumer reports. So there, oh yes, there's the pretty perspective on it from their anechoic data. We've actually predicted listener reactions to the loudspeaker. But we did 70 loudspeakers and in that 70 loudspeaker collection, there were big expensive speakers and there were little inexpensive speakers that had no bass.
cues.zh: 但回到这件事的动机源头，Consumer Reports。哦对，从他们的消声室数据可以看到漂亮的图景。我们实际上预测了听者对扬声器的反应。但我们做了70只扬声器，在这70只扬声器集合里，有又大又贵的扬声器，也有便宜的小扬声器，那些小扬声器没有低音。

cues.en: had no pretense to excellence, perhaps, but could be quite good over a smaller bandwidth, narrow bandwidth. So we separated out from that 70, 13, the original 13 that Consumers Union had published. And there's the result. On the left, these big dots here are the results of the listening tests, our double blind listening tests from the worst down here.
cues.zh: 也许并不以卓越为目标，但在较小带宽、窄带宽上可以相当好。所以我们从那70只中分出13只，就是 Consumers Union 最初发布的13只。结果在这里。左边这些大点，是听力测试的结果，我们的双盲听力测试，从最差的下边

cues.en: to the best up there. The open squares are the consumer reports ratings. And you can see our best is their worst. And this is a slightly negative correlation, but with a very low probability. So there's a lot of variation. And when we put it through the algorithm calculating algorithm that Sean had created,
cues.zh: 到最好的上边。空心方块是 Consumer Reports 的评分。你可以看到我们的最佳是他们的最差。这是轻微负相关，但概率很低。所以变化很大。当我们把它输入算法，也就是 Sean 创建的计算算法，

cues.en: The correlation was 0.995. Well, that's one. That's perfect. The calculated subjective ratings and the real subjective ratings just agreed. You can see they ran on the same line. Here's a very specific example, kind of an interesting one. There are four loudspeakers. These were all high-end, audiophile approved, highly regarded, reviewed loudspeakers.
cues.zh: 相关性为0.995。嗯，这就是1。完美。计算出的主观评分和真实主观评分完全一致。可以看到它们落在同一条线上。这里有个非常具体的例子，挺有意思。有四只扬声器。它们全都是高端、发烧友认可、备受推崇、被评测过的扬声器。

cues.en: If you followed these magazines and read these reviews, you would feel quite confident in going out. And if you had something of the order of $10,000 to spend, which is what these cost each pair, if you had that kind of money to spend, you would feel quite confident that if you bought any one of them, you'd be buying something resembling the state of the art. But in our listening tests,
cues.zh: 如果你关注这些杂志、读过这些评测，你会很有信心地出门选购。如果你有大约1万美元可花，这些每对就是这个价，如果你有那么多钱可花，你会很确信，无论买其中哪一对，买的都是接近最先进水平的东西。但在我们的听力测试中，

cues.en: They weren't all state of the art. There were two that were in a close horse race for first place, and the other two were just further down. And that's the spinorama data. And as they get flatter and smoother, the scores get higher. It's not magic. We would never, ever buy an electronic component. And nobody would ever design an electronic component that didn't have a frequency response that was flat from, you know...
cues.zh: 它们并非全都是顶尖水平。有两只在激烈争夺第一，另外两只则排得更靠后。这就是 Spinorama 数据。随着曲线越来越平坦、平滑，得分越来越高。这不是魔法。我们绝不会买一个电子元件。也没有人会设计一个频响不平直的电子元件，从，你知道……

cues.en: 10 Hz to 100 kHz. That kind of thing. It's flat and smooth. It's not difficult to do. And everybody does it. Why would we think that when you get to a loudspeaker, we can kind of throw that rule away? Well, it turns out that what our listeners here are doing is saying, no, you shouldn't throw that rule away. It's a good rule. Do it. And if you do it, your product's going to sound better. I will like it more.
cues.zh: 10 Hz 到 100 kHz。就这类东西。它平坦顺滑。做起来不难。大家都这么做。那为什么到了扬声器，我们就觉得可以抛弃这条规则？结果发现，我们这里的听众说的是：不，你不该抛弃这条规则。这是条好规则。照做。你照做了，产品就会听起来更好。我会更喜欢它。

cues.en: Looking at the, there were 350 listeners that participated in that test over three months or so period. 268 had done the test when Sean wrote his paper. It's in the journal of the AES. Showing how the listeners' performance of experience and background related to their performance. And their performance here was based on the FL statistics. It's a measure of how consistent people are when they...
cues.zh: 看一下，这个测试大约三个月里有 350 名听众参与。Sean 写论文时，其中 268 人已经完成了测试。论文发表在 AES 期刊上。展示了听众的经验和背景如何与他们的表现相关。而他们这里的表现基于 FL 统计量。它衡量的是人们有多一致，当他们……

cues.en: experience the same loudspeaker on different occasions because we do multiple times, they hear the speaker several times in different orders, different sequences. And on the strength of their differentiation, if they hear some loudspeakers that are from good to bad and they...
cues.zh: 在不同场合体验同一只扬声器时，因为我们会做多次，他们会在不同顺序、不同序列中听同一只扬声器好几次。而根据他们区分能力的强弱，如果他们听到一些从好到差的扬声器，而他们……

cues.en: you know give the good ones sixes and sevens and the bad ones twos and threes we know that's strong differentiation but there are people who don't have don't do that they will give you sixes and sevens and fives and sixes they don't really spread it out it turns out that the ones that exist exhibited both of these characteristics most are selected and trained listeners first of all is they're selected on the basis of having normal hearing
cues.zh: 你知道，给好的打六七分，给差的打两三分，我们知道这是很强的区分度。但有些人不会这么做；他们会给你打六七分和五六分，并没有真正拉开差距。结果发现，同时表现出这两种特征的人，大多数是经过筛选和训练的听众。首先，他们是基于拥有正常听力而被筛选出来的。

cues.en: not everybody has normal hearing. So that's the first hurdle they have to pass and then they are actually trained to recognize different kinds of defects. The retail sales people did quite well. The audio reviewers, six of them who volunteered to come in, they were bold people. They didn't do great. Our own brand sales and marketing people did really poorly.
cues.zh: 不是每个人都有正常听力。所以这是他们必须通过的第一道关，然后他们实际上会接受训练，识别不同类型的缺陷。零售销售人员做得相当好。音频评审员，有六位自愿来参加，他们是很勇敢的人。他们做得不算好。我们自己品牌的销售与市场人员做得真的很差。

cues.en: These are the type of people that are going out into the field saying, buy our product, it's great. I'll vouch for it. Please don't. And then the students, these are not students like you people in a music and sound recording environment. These are just generic students. Non-audio, non-music students. Anyway, it's kind of interesting. The point is though, look, they vary,
cues.zh: 这类人正是会跑到外面说：买我们的产品，它很棒。我担保。拜托别这样。然后是学生，这些不是像你们这样在音乐和录音环境里的学生。这些只是普通学生。非音频、非音乐专业的学生。总之，这挺有意思。但重点是，你看，他们有差异，

cues.en: They differed in their ability to give consistent answers and they differed in their abilities to give numerically spread out answers. But in the end, they all agreed on the ratings of those products. There were no inconsistencies. Humans are amazing measuring instruments. Amazing. I mean, I've done this for 40 years and I still kind of...
cues.zh: 他们在给出前后一致答案的能力上有差异，在给出数值上拉开差距的答案的能力上也有差异。但最终，他们对那些产品的评分都一致。没有不一致。人类是惊人的测量仪器。惊人。我是说，我做这行 40 年了，我还是有点……

cues.en: say, wow, this is remarkable. Because, as I say, you're listening to strange music, in a strange rhythm, strange loud speakers, and you're forming opinions. And the only way we can get those consistent opinions out of you is to not let you know what you're listening to. Do it blind. But if you know what you're listening to, I don't care what you think. It doesn't matter. And so, you know, I go back to Art Benéde's idea.
cues.zh: 比如说，哇，这真是太不可思议了。因为正如我所说，你听着奇怪的音乐，节奏很奇怪，扬声器也很奇怪，但你还是在形成自己的判断。而要让你给出一致的判断，唯一的方法就是不让你知道自己在听什么。进行盲听。但如果你知道自己在听什么，那我才不在乎你怎么想。这根本不重要。所以，我又想到了 Art Benéde 的观点。

cues.en: He was absolutely right, absolutely right. The difference is that we can measure loud speakers that are reproducing musical instruments. We don't have any parallel way to measure the musical instruments themselves, because they are so different and so varied and so peculiar in the way they radiate sound into rooms. So we have those two measurements now, and we combine them, and that gives us some psychoacoustic relationships. And what do we learn from that?
cues.zh: 他说得完全正确，完全正确。区别在于，我们可以测量重现乐器声音的扬声器。但我们没有任何类似的方法去测量乐器本身，因为乐器在向房间辐射声音时，差异非常大，变化非常多，而且各有各的特点。所以现在我们有了这两类测量结果，把它们结合起来，就能得到一些心理声学关系。那么我们从中了解到什么？

cues.en: is that to make a good loudspeaker, it has to be smooth and flat on axis. If you don't, people will complain. The directivity index should be smooth and relatively constant. It can change, but it should change gradually and smoothly, it seems. We're still in the learning process there, but that looks pretty good. We don't want any resonances. We've got to find in our measurements ways to identify
cues.zh: 那就是，要做出一只好的扬声器，它在轴向上的响应必须平滑且平直。否则，人们就会抱怨。指向性指数应该平滑，而且相对恒定。它可以变化，但看起来应该是逐渐、平滑地变化。我们还在不断摸索，但目前看来效果不错。我们不希望出现任何共振。我们必须从测量结果中找到识别共振的方法，

cues.en: and get rid of resonances, and we can do that in our spinaranas. And the reason why resonances are so important is because they are the building blocks of every sound that we care to listen to, human voices, and the sound of my voice is a bunch of resonances, musical instruments, just a bunch of resonances.
cues.zh: 并把共振消除掉，而我们可以在 Spinorama 测试中做到这一点。之所以共振如此重要，是因为共振是我们关注的各种声音的基本组成部分：人的声音，我的声音就是一堆共振；乐器的声音，也只是一堆共振。

cues.en: And so if you find additional resonances in loudspeakers, you're coloring the sound. And people recognize that quite quickly because that same coloration shows up in every recording, every music, every voice you play. So we want to get rid of that. So good loudspeakers are flat, probably constant in their radiation patterns that were the frequency range. They don't have resonances.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你在扬声器中发现额外的共振，就会给声音染上色彩。人们很快就能察觉到这一点，因为同样的染色会出现在你播放的每一段录音、每一首音乐和每一种人声中。所以我们要消除它。好的扬声器在整个频率范围内都应该是平直的，辐射模式可能也应该保持恒定，而且不能有共振。

cues.en: In order to do that, we have to measure at high resolution the old idea that third octave data is useful. I'm afraid if you have a third octave analyzer, give it to your kids, because it's a toy. And base performance, this is a big deal. Interesting. Base performance, all by Snowden accounts for about 30% of the factor weighting in the subjective evaluations. And if you don't get the base right,
